@devpanther Sorry for the inconvenience. The spec has been updated with those 2 edge cases:
```
Thera are 2 exceptions:
1. Issue solver shouldn't get issue commenter rewards
2. Issue creator shouldn't get issue commenter rewards
```

Check this [issue](https://github.com/rndquu-org/test-repo/issues/21)
When issue is solved then the following participants get rewards:
- issue creator
- issue solver
- issue commenter
When the same person creates an issue and comments in an issue then we need to generate 2 permits for that user (issue creator + issue commenter). We should consolidate such permits in a single one. So when an issue is closed then all permits should be grouped by users.
Thera are 2 exceptions:
1. Issue solver shouldn't get issue commenter rewards
2. Issue creator shouldn't get issue commenter rewards
What should be done:
- combine all generated permits by user
- remove [type](https://github.com/devpanther/bounty-bot/blob/6729f81eadc8504871657bdd432cc0621beef9ad/src/helpers/permit.ts#L60) from permit generation method (it was initially implemented [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/pull/692) as a kind of a hotfix) and use `keccak256(issue.node_id . bountyHunter.node_id)` for permit nonces
- combined permits should have a caption that states the reason behind the generated permit, ex: "Issue creator and issue solver rewards"

In the early days of the github REST API all entities (issue, user, comment, etc...) used the `id` property. As far as I understand `issue.id`, `user.id` and `comment.id` can intersect while the `node_id` property is globally unique across all entities. That is why [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot/blob/08a2dfb1ffbf426fd984a97fe583a310a7c1e43a/src/handlers/payout/action.ts#L186) `issue.node_id` was used. 
The 2nd useful thing regarding the `node_id` property is that some APIs are missing from the github REST API while exist in the graphql API where you can fetch entities by `node_id`.
That is why I think it is better to use `node_id` whenever possible compared to the `id` property.

Currently I feel like the code is messy and unreadable. Could you refactor it to make it easier to read? I feel like the names for some variables and functions are off.
Ideally I'd like to see a top level function `incentivesCalculation` that first checks if all conditions are met (not empty private key, issued closed as completed, is bounty, autopay is not off, and so on), then it should get all the issue comments (to avoid retrieving them multiple times). 
After that it should call three function `calculateIssueCreatorReward`, `calculateIssueConversationReward` and `calculateIssueAssigneeReward`, all of them receive comments and return something like `{ user_id, username, reward }[]`, then the main function can aggregate all rewards together, apply multipliers, deduct penalties, retrieve user's wallet and generate permits.
I hope you understand what I mean. Let me know if you have questions
